questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{75}x,\, & 5\le x\le 10 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<5 \\ h(x),\, & 5\le x\le 10 \\ 1,\, & x>10.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the function $h(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $5\le x\le 10,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<5 \\ {\int }_{5}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & 5\le x\le 10 \\ 1, & x>10\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{5}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{5}^{x}\frac{2}{75}t\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={\frac{1}{75}{t}^{2}|}_{5}^{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{75}{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}-25}{75}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<5, \\ \frac{{x}^{2}-25}{75},\, & 5\le x\le 10, \\ 1,\, & x>10.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{25}, & 0\le x\le 5 \\ 1, & x>5,\end{aligned}
$$

find $P(1\le X\le 3).$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that for continuous random variables, it doesn't matter whether or not we include the endpoints of the interval. So we can perform the computation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1\le X\le 3) & =P(1<X\le 3) \\  & =P(X\le 3)-P(X\le 1) \\  & =F(3)-F(1) \\  & =\frac{{3}^{2}}{25}-\frac{{1}^{2}}{25} \\  & =\frac{8}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{3{x}^{2}}{\pi (1+{x}^{6})},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

find the cumulative distribution function $F(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{3{t}^{2}}{\pi (1+{t}^{6})}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\frac{\operatorname{arctan}⁡({t}^{3})}{\pi }|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{\pi }+\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ \frac{x}{6}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{1458}, & 0\le x\le 9 \\ 1, & x>9,\end{aligned}
$$

find $P(1<X\le 3).$
questions.worked_solution:
We can perform this computation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<X\le 3) & =P(X\le 3)-P(X\le 1) \\  & =F(3)-F(1) \\  & =(\frac{3}{6}-\frac{{3}^{3}}{1458})-(\frac{1}{6}-\frac{{1}^{3}}{1458}) \\  & =\frac{230}{729}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{{e}^{-|x|}}{2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

its cumulative distribution function is

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{x}}{2},\, & x\le 0 \\ h(x),\, & x>0\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{{e}^{t}}{2}\,\text{d}t, & x<0 \\ {\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{t}}{2}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-t}}{2}\,\text{d}t, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute the integrals.

- If $x\le 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{{e}^{t}}{2}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{t}}{2}|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{t}}{2}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- If $x>0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-t}}{2}\,\text{d}t & =-{\frac{{e}^{-t}}{2}|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-x}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{t}}{2}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-t}}{2}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{{e}^{-x}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =1-\frac{{e}^{-x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{x}}{2},\, & x\le 0 \\ 1-\frac{{e}^{-x}}{2},\, & x>0.\end{aligned}
$$
